checklist.step: Open the market-entry request and fix the state/line/product scope
actions: Open Market Entry ▸ New Request and record: writing company legal name, NAIC company code and FEIN, target jurisdiction (rep: Rhode Island), product family Annuity Contracts (non-group) and planned first-write date.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the specific contract forms in scope (fixed deferred, MYGA, indexed, immediate) and paste the form numbers and edition dates onto the request.
Ask the Head of Distribution which channel will solicit the state (career agency, independent producer, bank/broker-dealer) so the downstream producer training and appointment work can be sized.
Attach the signed entry business case and name the request <company>-<state>-annuity-<yyyy-mm>.
checklist.done: the request carries company, NAIC code, jurisdiction, annuity form numbers, channel and planned first-write date, with the business case attached.

checklist.step: Pull the company's current Certificate of Authority for the target state
actions: Open the Certificate of Authority register and filter Company = writing company, State = Rhode Island; download the stored certificate PDF.
Read off the certificate: issue date, continuation/expiry date, and the exact lines of authority as printed (e.g. Life, Annuities, Accident & Health, Variable Annuities).
Where no certificate is on file, or the PDF pre-dates the last continuation, request a certified copy from the Rhode Island DBR Insurance Division company licensing unit before going further.
Save the certificate into the entry folder as <state>-CoA-<issue date>.pdf.
checklist.done: a current, dated certificate PDF for the target state sits in the entry folder with its lines of authority transcribed.

checklist.step: Map the annuity product to a line of authority on the certificate
actions: Open the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix for Life/Annuity and locate the TOI and Sub-TOI for the specific annuity contract (e.g. A02I Individual Annuities — Deferred Non-Variable).
Write on the entry request which certificate line of authority carries that TOI, quoting the line wording from the certificate verbatim.
Flag separately any indexed or variable feature — variable annuities need the variable line plus a registered separate account, and cannot ride on the plain Annuities line.
Where the TOI has no matching line on the certificate, set the request status to 'Expansion required' and stop the write gate from opening.
checklist.done: each in-scope annuity TOI is mapped to a quoted certificate line, or the request is marked 'Expansion required'.

checklist.step: Confirm company status independently at the NAIC and the state DOI
actions: In NAIC iSite+ open the Company Demographics / State Licensing screen for the NAIC company code and read the licence status and lines held in the target state.
Open the Rhode Island DBR Insurance Division company search on the state site and pull the public licence record for the same company.
Compare all three sources (certificate PDF, iSite+, DOI lookup) field by field on status, lines and continuation date; any mismatch goes to Regulatory Counsel the same day.
Print both lookups to PDF dated the day of the check and file them in the entry folder — these are the evidence behind the coverage call.
checklist.done: certificate, NAIC iSite+ and the DOI public record agree on status and lines, with both lookups captured and dated.

checklist.step: Check the licence continuation and fee position for the state
actions: Read the continuation/renewal date off the certificate and the DOI invoice or bulletin that sets the annual company licence continuation fee.
Confirm with the Controller that the current-year continuation fee and any premium tax prepayment for the state have been paid, and get the payment reference.
Load the continuation date into the CoA register with a 90-day-before reminder so the authority cannot lapse mid-year.
Where the continuation is unpaid or in dispute, hold the entry — an expired authority is the same as no authority.
checklist.done: the continuation date is in the register with a reminder, and the current-year fee payment reference is recorded.

checklist.step: Open a UCAA Expansion Application where the annuity line is missing
actions: Download the current UCAA Expansion Application package and the target state's UCAA State Specific Requirements checklist from the NAIC UCAA page.

Assemble the package: Application Form, plan of operation for the annuity line, the most recent audited and statutory financial statements, Certificate of Compliance and Certificate of Deposit from the domiciliary state, and NAIC Biographical Affidavits (third-party verified) for officers and directors.
Confirm the state's minimum capital and surplus and statutory deposit for the annuity line, and get Treasury to evidence the deposit before submission.
Submit to the state's company licensing unit per its stated channel, record the acknowledgement date, and diary the review window (commonly 60–90 days from a complete filing).
Report the expected approval date back to the entry request so the first-write date can be re-planned.
checklist.done: a complete UCAA expansion package is submitted and acknowledged, with the review window and revised first-write date on the entry request.

checklist.step: Confirm the annuity forms and rates are approved for use in the state
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access and search by company NAIC code, state and the annuity form numbers taken from the entry request.
Confirm each form and its edition date carries a disposition of Approved / Filed for that state, and copy the SERFF Tracking Number and disposition date onto the entry request.
Where any in-scope form is unfiled or pending, mark that form 'not writable' and exclude it from the write-gate release rather than delaying the whole entry.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen to PDF into the entry folder.
checklist.done: every annuity form to be written in the state has an approved SERFF disposition and tracking number on the entry request.

checklist.step: Confirm the producer-side pre-use gate for the state before any solicitation
actions: List the state's producer requirements for this line: resident/non-resident licence with the Life (and, where applicable, Variable) line of authority, the state's annuity suitability/best-interest training (typically a one-time 4-credit course), and the carrier's product-specific training for the annuity contracts being launched.

Confirm the product-specific training module for these exact form numbers exists in the LMS and is published to the state's producer population; if not, raise it with the Learning Development Manager with the launch date.
Set the LMS completion requirement so no producer can be released to solicit in the state without both the state annuity training and the carrier product-specific training recorded.
Write the required-training list onto the entry request as a release precondition.
checklist.done: the state's annuity training and the carrier product-specific module are published in the LMS and set as a release precondition on the entry request.

checklist.step: Confirm the appointment path and channel readiness for the state
actions: In NIPR Gateway confirm the writing company is set up to transact appointments in the target state and that the company's NIPR billing account can fund that state's appointment fees.

Check the state's appointment rules for the Life/Annuity line: whether appointment must precede solicitation, and the number of days after the first application in which the appointment must be filed.
Confirm the agency (firm) entity licences and appointments are in place where the channel sells through agencies, not only the individual producers.
Record the appointment path and fee per producer on the entry request so Distribution can size the launch.
checklist.done: NIPR is set up for the company in the state, and the appointment rule, path and per-producer fee are recorded on the entry request.

checklist.step: Set the write gate in the policy administration system
actions: In the product/state availability configuration, keep the target state closed for every in-scope annuity plan code until the entry request reaches 'Released'.
Configure the state's earliest-issue date on each plan code to the released first-write date, so back-dated applications cannot slip through.
Add a hard edit that rejects any annuity application in the state where the writing agent's licence or appointment status is not 'Active' in the producer management system.
Have the Business Systems Analyst evidence the edit with a rejected test application and file the screenshot in the entry folder.
checklist.done: the state is closed for the annuity plan codes until release, with an evidenced hard edit blocking unlicensed writing agents.

checklist.step: Write the coverage determination into the Certificate of Authority register
actions: Add a register row per company/state/line: certificate number, issue date, continuation date, quoted line of authority, mapped TOI/Sub-TOI, coverage decision Yes/No, decider and decision date.
Link the row to the entry folder holding the certificate PDF, the dated iSite+ and DOI captures and the SERFF dispositions.
Set the row status to 'Covered — pending counsel' where the line mapping needed judgement, otherwise 'Covered — closed'.
Leave any 'Expansion required' row open with the UCAA acknowledgement date attached.
checklist.done: one complete, source-linked register row exists per company/state/line with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel sign-off before the state is opened
actions: Route to counsel every entry where the annuity TOI was mapped to a line by interpretation rather than an exact wording match, and every entry involving indexed or variable features.
Counsel re-reads the state's certificate-of-authority statute and the certificate wording and confirms or overturns the coverage call in writing on the register row.
Overturned rows go back to the Regulatory Filing Specialist and the state stays closed until an expansion is filed.
Confirmed rows are stamped with counsel name and date and moved to 'Covered — closed'.
checklist.done: no interpreted or variable-feature coverage call is closed without a dated counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Release the state to distribution with an explicit earliest-write date
actions: Publish the release memo to the channel naming the state, the writable annuity plan codes and form editions, and the earliest-write date.
Open the state on the producer management system's territory/appointment configuration only for producers whose licence, appointment and product training are all 'Complete'.
Brief the field via the Broker & Agent Portal bulletin that solicitation in the state before the earliest-write date is prohibited, naming the plan codes excluded.
Record the release memo reference on the entry request and close it.
checklist.done: the channel has a dated release memo, the state is open only to fully qualified producers, and the entry request is closed.

checklist.step: Escalate when the first-write date cannot survive the state's licensing timeline
actions: Compare the planned first-write date against the UCAA review window, the SERFF approval position and the producer training lead time for every open entry, weekly.
Where the date is unreachable, escalate to the Head of Compliance and the product sponsor within one business day.
Put the options in writing: move the launch date, launch in the covered lines only, or drop the state — writing outside the certificate is never an option.
Record the decision, its owner and the revised date on the register row.
checklist.done: every unreachable first-write date has a written, owned decision that keeps the state either compliant or out of the launch.

checklist.step: Retain the market-entry evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the entry folder (certificate PDF, dated iSite+ and DOI captures, UCAA package and acknowledgement, SERFF dispositions, counsel sign-off, release memo) into the repository under Licensing & Appointments ▸ Market Entry ▸ <state> ▸ <year>.
Apply the 7-years-from-withdrawal-of-authority retention label so the record survives an exit from the state.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by NAIC company code, state, line of authority and annuity form number.
checklist.done: the entry record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by company code, state and line.

testing.step: Build the population of state/line pairs actually written in the period
actions: Extract every annuity contract issued in the period with issue date, writing company, situs state, plan code, form number/edition and first premium.
Collapse to distinct writing company × state × annuity TOI pairs and record the contract count and premium behind each pair.
Reconcile total issued premium in the extract to the period's statutory Exhibit 1 annuity considerations by state and clear any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the state/line population is reconciled to reported annuity considerations by state and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Join every written pair to a current Certificate of Authority row
actions: Join each written company × state × TOI pair to the CoA register on company code and state, and check the mapped line covers the TOI.
Check the certificate's issue date precedes, and its continuation date follows, the earliest and latest issue dates in the pair.
List every unjoined pair, every lapsed-continuation pair and every pair covered only by an 'Expansion required' row as automatic exceptions with the contract count and premium attached.
testing.done: every written pair is matched to a certificate in force across the whole writing window, or listed as an exception with its exposure quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of market entries opened in the period and 100% of pairs where the annuity line was mapped by interpretation or carries an indexed/variable feature.
Take 20 further written pairs at random (seeded, reproducible) weighted by premium, for a minimum of 30 sampled pairs.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every period market entry and every interpreted line mapping.

testing.step: Re-perform the licence status check at the NAIC and the state DOI
actions: For each sampled pair, open NAIC iSite+ Company Demographics ▸ State Licensing for the company code and read the lines held in that state.
Repeat the lookup on the state DOI's public company search (rep: Rhode Island DBR Insurance Division) and reach your own coverage conclusion before opening the register row.
Compare to the recorded determination; a right answer supported by the wrong line wording is still an exception.
Screenshot both lookups into the workpaper with the retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled pair has an independent coverage conclusion from two sources with dated captures.

testing.step: Re-test the TOI-to-line mapping against the NAIC coding matrix
actions: Look up each sampled plan code's annuity TOI/Sub-TOI in the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix and compare it to the TOI recorded on the register row.
Confirm indexed and variable products are not being carried on a plain Annuities line, and that variable products have a registered separate account behind them.
Flag miscoded rows — a wrong TOI usually means the wrong line of authority was read as sufficient.
testing.done: TOI, Sub-TOI and certificate line agree with the coding matrix for every sampled pair, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Trace forms actually issued to an approved SERFF filing for the state
actions: For each sampled pair, take the annuity form numbers and edition dates from the issued contracts, not from the entry request.
In SERFF Filing Access search company, state and form number, and confirm an Approved / Filed disposition dated before the earliest issue date.
Where no approved filing exists for the edition actually issued, raise it as a breach separate from the CoA finding.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled form edition traces to an approved SERFF disposition pre-dating first issue, or a separate breach is raised.

testing.step: Test the producer-side pre-use gate on the sampled states
actions: For each sampled state, pull the LMS completion extract for the carrier annuity product-specific module and the state annuity suitability training for producers who wrote in the period.
Match each writing agent on the sampled contracts to a completion date that pre-dates the application signature date.
Attempt a negative test: submit a test application in the policy administration system for a producer with no product training and confirm the hard edit rejects it.
Any contract written by a producer without pre-dated training is an exception regardless of the CoA position.
testing.done: every sampled writing agent has pre-dated product and state annuity training, and the blocking edit is evidenced as working.

testing.step: Recompute the continuation and expansion date maths
actions: For each sampled state, recompute the licence continuation window from the certificate issue/continuation dates and confirm no issue date falls outside it.
For entries that required a UCAA expansion, compare the acknowledgement date, the approval date and the actual first-write date, and confirm the first write followed approval.
Confirm the current-year continuation fee payment reference exists for every sampled state and matches the ledger.
Any business written between a lapse and a reinstatement is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled state was written during a lapse or before an expansion approval, and continuation payments reconcile to the ledger.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying the company code, state, TOI, contract count, premium written and the date range of the exposure.
Assign a root cause (line mapped by interpretation, continuation lapsed, expansion not filed, write gate opened early, training module not published) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for business written outside the certificate, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and quantify potential rescission or premium refund.
Carry every open exception into the next test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, quantified exposure, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate by pair and by premium and compare to the zero-uncovered-write threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Licensing & Appointments and with no involvement in any sampled entry — sign the workpaper.
Report results and any self-reports to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under Licensing & Appointments ▸ CoA Coverage Test.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate by premium and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Take in the contracting request and capture the producer's identifiers
actions: Open Contracting ▸ New Producer and record legal name, NPN, SSN/FEIN, resident state, agency/FMO hierarchy and the states requested for solicitation.
Get the requested product set from the Agency Relations Manager and confirm it includes Annuity Contracts (non-group) so the annuity training track is triggered.
Reject the request at intake if the NPN is missing or does not resolve — every downstream check keys on the NPN.
Attach the signed producer agreement and the W-9 to the contracting file.
checklist.done: the contracting file carries a resolving NPN, the requested state list and the annuity product set, with the signed agreement attached.

checklist.step: Verify the licence and lines of authority in the NIPR Producer Database
actions: In NIPR Gateway run a PDB Report by NPN and open the Licenses section for each requested state.
Confirm for each state a licence status of Active with a Life line of authority (and Variable Life/Variable Annuity where the product requires it) and an expiry date beyond today.
Read the Regulatory Actions and Appointments sections and record any administrative action, suspension or revocation for review by the Producer Compliance Manager.
Save the PDB report PDF into the contracting file named <NPN>-PDB-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf — this is the licence evidence of record.
checklist.done: a dated PDB report is filed showing an Active licence with the required lines in every requested state, and any regulatory action is flagged.

checklist.step: Resolve licence gaps before anything is promised to the producer
actions: Where a requested state shows no licence, use NIPR Gateway ▸ Non-Resident Licensing to send the producer the application link for that state and record the transaction id.
Track the state's issuance turnaround and keep the state in 'Pending licence' on the contracting file until PDB shows Active.
Where a licence is Inactive or Expired, tell the Agency Relations Manager in writing that the state cannot be released and remove it from the launch list.
Never mark a state releasable on the strength of an application receipt — only on a PDB Active status.
checklist.done: every requested state is either PDB-Active or explicitly held in 'Pending licence' with a NIPR transaction id.

checklist.step: Assign the carrier annuity product-specific training
actions: Assign the product-specific module covering the exact annuity contracts to be sold — contract form numbers, surrender charge schedule and period, market value adjustment, index crediting methods and caps/participation rates, free-withdrawal provisions, death benefit and annuitization options.
Set the assignment due date to at least 5 business days before the producer's planned first solicitation date supplied by Distribution.
Confirm the module carries an assessment with a stated pass mark and issues a timestamped completion certificate.
Where a new annuity form or a material rate/feature change launches, re-assign the module to the whole state population before the launch date.
checklist.done: the producer holds an LMS assignment for the exact annuity forms in scope with a due date before first solicitation.

checklist.step: Assign and evidence the state annuity suitability/best-interest training
actions: For each requested state, record whether the state has adopted the NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model and its one-time annuity training requirement (commonly a 4-credit course) plus any best-interest supplement.
Check the producer's CE transcript in the PDB or the state CE vendor record for an existing annuity training credit and its completion date before assigning a duplicate course.
Where absent, direct the producer to a state-approved provider course and load the completion certificate and credit-bank reference into the LMS record.
For any long-term-care rider on an annuity, add the state's LTC training (commonly an 8-hour initial course) to the requirement list.
checklist.done: each requested state shows either an existing verified annuity training credit or a newly filed state-approved completion certificate.

checklist.step: Verify training completion is real and matched to the right producer
actions: Pull the LMS completion record and check it carries NPN, module version, completion timestamp, assessment score and pass mark.
Spot-check the state annuity training certificate against the state CE transcript or the provider's verification portal — a producer-supplied PDF alone is not verification.
Reject completions recorded against a name-only match; re-key to the NPN so the record survives a name change.
File the verified certificates in the contracting file.
checklist.done: every training completion is NPN-keyed, timestamped and independently verified against the provider or CE transcript.

checklist.step: Set the solicitation eligibility flag per producer per state
actions: Set Eligible-to-Solicit = Yes for a state only when PDB shows Active with the required lines AND the carrier product module AND the state annuity training are all complete.
Stamp the eligibility effective date and the evidence references (PDB report name, LMS completion ids) onto the producer's state row.
Leave every other state at Not Eligible with the blocking reason spelled out (no licence, training outstanding, regulatory action under review).
Push the eligibility table to the policy administration system nightly so the application edit reads current status.
checklist.done: each producer/state row shows an eligibility decision with its evidence references, and the nightly push to policy admin succeeded.

checklist.step: Block solicitation and application intake for ineligible producers
actions: Configure the annuity new-business intake to reject any application whose writing agent NPN is not Eligible-to-Solicit in the application's signature state on the signature date.
Make the edit read the signature date, not the received date, so a back-dated application cannot pass.
Route rejects to a Licensing Ops work queue with the failing reason (licence / product training / state annuity training) shown to the processor.
Evidence the edit quarterly with a deliberate test application and file the screenshot.
checklist.done: the intake edit rejects ineligible NPNs on signature date and the reject queue shows the specific failing requirement.

checklist.step: Close off the Broker & Agent Portal and lead flow for ineligible producers
actions: Restrict the portal's annuity illustration and quoting tools to producers flagged Eligible-to-Solicit in the state selected on the quote screen.
Suppress annuity marketing collateral downloads and lead assignments for states where the producer is Not Eligible.
Post the state-by-state requirement summary (licence line, carrier module, state annuity training) on the portal so producers can self-serve their gaps.
Notify the Agency Relations Manager weekly of producers blocked for more than 21 days.
checklist.done: quoting, illustrations and leads are unavailable in states where the producer is not eligible, and long-blocked producers are escalated weekly.

checklist.step: Run the daily PDB delta and suspend lapsed producers same day
actions: Subscribe the full producer roster to NIPR Alerts / PDB Reports so licence status changes, expirations and regulatory actions arrive daily.
Load the delta file and auto-flip Eligible-to-Solicit to No for any NPN whose licence moved to Expired, Inactive, Suspended or Revoked in any state.
Work the exception list within one business day: contact the producer, confirm renewal in flight, and hold the state closed until PDB returns to Active.
Log every suspension with the date, state and the trigger record from the delta file.
checklist.done: the daily delta is loaded, lapsed producers are suspended the same business day, and each suspension is logged with its trigger.

checklist.step: Re-verify eligibility immediately before requesting an appointment
actions: Before submitting any appointment transaction, re-run the PDB report for the NPN and re-read the state licence status as of that day.
Confirm the carrier annuity product training and state annuity training are still recorded complete and not expired by a refresher requirement.
Abort the appointment request where anything has changed since contracting and return the file to the eligibility queue.
Attach the re-verification PDB report to the appointment request record.
checklist.done: every appointment request carries a same-day PDB re-verification and a current training position.

checklist.step: Withhold and claw back commission where eligibility failed
actions: Configure the commission run to place on hold any annuity commission whose writing agent was not Eligible-to-Solicit in the state on the application signature date.
Report held items weekly to the Producer Compliance Manager with policy number, NPN, state, premium and commission amount.
Release only after eligibility is evidenced as having existed at signature, or process a chargeback where it did not.
Record every release or chargeback decision with its approver on the held item.
checklist.done: commission on ineligible-producer business is held automatically and each release or chargeback carries a named approver.

checklist.step: Decide the treatment of business already written by an ineligible producer
actions: Assemble the exposure: policy count, premium, states and the exact eligibility defect (licence lapsed, product training missing, state annuity training missing).

Read the state's unlicensed-activity and producer-training provisions (rep: Alabama Department of Insurance requirements) and decide whether the contracts stand, need re-signature by an eligible producer, or require rescission and premium return.
Decide the self-report position per state and draft the notification where required.
Record the decision, the statutory basis and the customer-remediation plan on the exception record.
checklist.done: every block of ineligible-producer business has a counsel decision with a statutory basis and a customer remediation plan.

checklist.step: Re-train the state population when an annuity product changes materially
actions: Take the change notice from the Insurance Product Manager (new form edition, changed surrender schedule, new index crediting method, changed caps or bonus structure).
Update the product module content and version it so completions of the prior version are distinguishable in reporting.
Re-assign the new version to every producer eligible in the affected states with a due date before the product's effective date, and gate solicitation of the new form on the new version.
Report completion percentage by state weekly to the Producer Compliance Manager until the population is clear.
checklist.done: the changed annuity form cannot be solicited until the producer holds the current module version, tracked to completion by state.

checklist.step: Retain the producer eligibility evidence
actions: File per NPN: signed producer agreement, dated PDB reports, carrier module completion certificates with version, state annuity training certificates and CE transcript captures.
Apply the 5-years-after-termination retention label so the pack survives the producer leaving.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by NPN, producer name, state and annuity form number for a market conduct producer-list request.
checklist.done: each producer has a retained, labelled eligibility pack retrievable by NPN and state.

testing.step: Build the population of annuity applications and their writing agents
actions: Extract every annuity application signed in the quarter with application number, signature date, signature state, plan code/form edition, writing agent NPN and premium.
Add all producers newly contracted or reinstated in the quarter from the producer management system so onboarding files are covered too.
Reconcile the application count and premium to the quarter's new-business production report and clear differences before sampling.
testing.done: the application population reconciles to the new-business production report and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every application to an eligibility position dated on or before signature
actions: Join each application to the producer's state eligibility history on NPN + signature state and read the status as at the signature date.
Check the carrier product module completion date and the state annuity training date both pre-date the signature date.
List every application with no eligibility row, a Not Eligible status at signature, or training dated after signature as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every application is matched to an eligibility position pre-dating signature or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of applications written by producers reinstated during the quarter and 100% written within 30 days of the producer's first eligibility date.
Take 25 further applications at random (seeded, reproducible) spread across at least 10 states including Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona, for a minimum of 40 sampled applications.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers the newly-eligible and reinstated producer strata.

testing.step: Re-perform the licence check in the NIPR PDB for each sampled application
actions: Run a PDB report by NPN and open the Licenses section, reading the licence effective and expiry dates for the application's signature state.
Reach your own conclusion on whether the licence and lines of authority were Active on the signature date before opening the contracting file.
Compare to the recorded eligibility decision; an Active licence lacking the required Life or variable line is still a fail.
Screenshot the PDB Licenses section with the retrieval date into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled application has an independent PDB conclusion for its signature state with a dated capture.

testing.step: Trace the carrier product training to a real completion for the form sold
actions: Open the LMS completion record for the sampled NPN and confirm the module version covers the exact annuity form edition on the application.
Check the completion timestamp, assessment score against the stated pass mark, and that the record is NPN-keyed rather than name-matched.
Where the product changed mid-quarter, confirm the producer completed the current version before soliciting the new form.
Treat a completion of a superseded module version for a materially changed product as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled application traces to an NPN-keyed completion of the module version covering the form actually sold.

testing.step: Verify the state annuity training credit at the source
actions: For each sampled state requiring annuity training, verify the producer's credit on the state CE transcript or the approved provider's verification portal rather than the stored PDF.
Confirm the course was state-approved for the signature state and completed before the signature date.
Where an LTC rider was attached, confirm the state's LTC training requirement was met as well.
Any credit that cannot be verified at source is an exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled state annuity training credit is confirmed at the CE transcript or provider source and pre-dates signature.

testing.step: Test that the intake edit actually blocks ineligible producers
actions: Submit three test annuity applications: one with a lapsed licence NPN, one with no carrier product training, one back-dated to a date before the producer's eligibility date.
Confirm all three are rejected and land in the Licensing Ops queue with the correct failing reason displayed.
Confirm the edit reads the signature date by checking the back-dated case specifically.
Capture the reject screens and the queue entries into the workpaper.
testing.done: all three negative tests reject with the correct reason and the signature-date logic is evidenced.

testing.step: Recompute the suspension timeliness from the daily PDB delta
actions: Take every licence lapse in the quarter from the NIPR delta files and compute the elapsed business days between the delta date and the eligibility flip to No.
Confirm no application was signed by that NPN in that state between the lapse date and the suspension.
Recompute the reinstatement side: no eligibility restored before PDB returned to Active.
Any application signed during a lapse window is a reportable unlicensed-activity breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every lapse was suspended within one business day and no application was signed inside a lapse window.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with application number, NPN, signature state, premium, the failing requirement and the commission paid.
Assign a root cause (PDB not re-verified, training assigned late, module version stale, delta not worked, edit bypassed by manual entry) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date, confirm commission was held or clawed back, and refer unlicensed-activity cases to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report decision.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, a commission disposition and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate by application and by premium and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Licensing Ops and Distribution — sign the workpaper.
Report results, unlicensed-activity breaches and self-report decisions to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under Licensing & Appointments ▸ Producer Eligibility Test.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — each state's appointment and termination-for-cause statute read alongside the state's producer product-training requirement (rep: Alabama Department of Insurance (ALDOI); Arkansas and Arizona equivalents reviewed for the same population)

In-scope processes.value: Appointment filing on first annuity application or contract execution, appointment renewal, and termination filing (including for-cause reporting) across all 51 jurisdictions for Annuity Contracts (non-group) producers

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway Appointment/Termination transactions (single and bulk) with per-state fee funding; transaction ids and statuses written back to the agency/producer management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Appointment & Termination Processing Procedure — per-state day-count table, trigger events (first application signature, contract execution, channel move, cause event), NIPR submission and rejection handling, producer notification of termination

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Producer Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel; the per-state day-count table is re-validated annually against the NIPR appointment/termination state requirements and on any state bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — appointment filed within the state's window from the trigger (commonly 15 days from contract execution or the first application, up to 30 days in some states); termination filed within the state's window (commonly 30 days of the termination effective date) with written notice to the producer within the state's separate window (commonly 15 days of the filing)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Producer management system SLA clocks per pending appointment at day 3, day 7 and day 10 against the shortest applicable state window; termination clocks at day 5, day 15 and day 25; overdue items page the Producer Compliance Manager daily

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every appointment or termination filed after the state window closes is logged with the NPN, state, trigger date, filed date, days late and whether a late fee or state notification was required

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late filing remediation and every for-cause termination narrative before it is transmitted to the state

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All appointment and termination transactions with a trigger date in the quarter, plus all producer relationship end-dates in the producer management system whether or not a termination was filed

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Appointments and terminations filed within window ≥ 99%, with zero tolerance on for-cause terminations and on any producer who wrote business in a state with no appointment on file; any for-cause miss escalates to the Head of Compliance

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly appointment/termination timeliness workpaper (trigger population, NIPR transaction traces, day-count recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-state appointment and termination registers with NIPR transaction ids, effective dates and producer notice dates, producible for a state DOI appointment audit within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state appointment/termination enquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears every for-cause narrative and any admission of a late or missed termination filing

checklist.step: Maintain the per-state appointment and termination day-count table
actions: Build one row per jurisdiction holding: appointment trigger (contract execution vs first application), appointment filing window in days, whether appointment must precede solicitation, termination filing window, for-cause reporting requirement and the producer-notice window.
Validate each row against the NIPR appointment and termination state requirement pages and the state's producer licensing statute, and cite the source on the row.
Re-validate the whole table annually and within 10 business days of any state bulletin affecting appointments.
Publish the table to the producer management system so SLA clocks compute from the correct window per state.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction has a cited, current row and the producer management system computes SLA clocks from it.

checklist.step: Detect the appointment trigger the day it occurs
actions: Run the daily trigger report: producer agreements executed yesterday, and first annuity applications received in a state where the writing agent has no active appointment.
For application-triggered states, take the application signature date — not the received date — as the clock start and write it on the pending appointment row.
For contract-triggered states, take the counter-signature date from the executed producer agreement in DocuSign.
Open a pending appointment task per NPN per state with the trigger date, the state window and the computed due date.
checklist.done: every trigger from the prior day has a pending appointment task carrying its trigger date, window and due date.

checklist.step: Confirm licence and product training before submitting the appointment
actions: Re-run the PDB report for the NPN and confirm an Active licence with the Life/annuity lines in the appointment state as of today.
Confirm the carrier annuity product-specific training and the state annuity training are recorded complete in the LMS.
Where either fails, keep the SLA clock running, flag the blocking reason on the task and escalate to the Agency Relations Manager the same day — the state window does not pause for internal gaps.
Attach the PDB report to the pending appointment task.
checklist.done: no appointment is submitted without a same-day PDB Active status and complete training, and blocked tasks are escalated the same day.

checklist.step: Submit the appointment transaction in NIPR Gateway
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ Submit and select the state, the writing company's NAIC code and the line of authority the annuity product requires.
Enter the NPN, the appointment effective date (the trigger date where the state back-dates to it) and the appointment type (individual or agency/firm).
Confirm the state's appointment fee is funded from the company's NIPR account before submitting — an unfunded transaction does not count as filed.
Record the NIPR transaction id and submission timestamp on the pending appointment task.
checklist.done: the appointment is submitted with the correct state, company, line and effective date, and the transaction id is on the task.

checklist.step: Work NIPR rejections inside the original state window
actions: Check the NIPR transaction status daily and open every Rejected item to read the state's reason code (name mismatch, licence not active, wrong line, fee shortfall, duplicate appointment).
Correct and resubmit the same day; the SLA clock keeps running against the original trigger date, not the resubmission.
Where the rejection is a state-side data problem, contact the state DOI licensing unit, log the contact date and the person spoken to, and keep the record as the timeliness defence.
Only mark the task complete on a NIPR status of Accepted/Active with an effective date.
checklist.done: every rejection is corrected and resubmitted the same day, and tasks close only on an Accepted status with an effective date.

checklist.step: Write appointment status back to the systems that gate business
actions: Load the NIPR appointment feed nightly and update each producer/state row with appointment status, effective date and transaction id.
Push the appointment position to the Policy Administration Platform so the annuity intake edit reads current appointment as well as licence status.
Reconcile the loaded record count to the NIPR feed control total and raise a data ticket on any variance.
Alert Licensing Ops on any producer writing business in a state where the appointment is Pending or Rejected.
checklist.done: appointment status is current in the producer and policy admin systems nightly, with feed counts reconciled.

checklist.step: Detect and classify the termination trigger
actions: Run the daily termination trigger report: producer agreements terminated, channel or agency moves, deaths, retirements, and cases referred by Compliance or SIU.
Classify each as without cause or for cause, taking the classification from the Producer Compliance Manager, not from the field manager requesting the termination.
Set the termination effective date and compute the state filing due date and the separate producer-notice due date from the day-count table.
Open a termination task per NPN per appointed state — a producer appointed in 30 states generates 30 tasks.
checklist.done: every termination trigger has a classification, an effective date and per-state filing and notice due dates.

checklist.step: Build the for-cause narrative and clear it with counsel
actions: Take the underlying file from Compliance or SIU: what the producer did, the dates, the customers affected and the evidence relied on.
Draft the reportable-activity statement against the state's listed for-cause grounds (misappropriation, forgery, misrepresentation, unlicensed activity, fraud, felony conviction).
Confirm the facts are stated, not characterised, and that the statement is supportable if the producer challenges it — states extend immunity only to reports made without malice.
Sign off the narrative and record the sign-off date on the termination task before any transmission.
checklist.done: every for-cause narrative is fact-based, mapped to a statutory ground and carries a dated counsel sign-off before transmission.

checklist.step: File the termination in NIPR within the state window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ Terminate, select the state and company, and enter the NPN, termination effective date and reason code.
For for-cause terminations attach or transmit the counsel-cleared narrative by the channel the state requires, and note where the state demands a separate written report to the commissioner.
Submit before the state's filing due date (commonly 30 days from the termination effective date) and record the transaction id and timestamp.
Confirm acceptance and file the confirmation against the task.
checklist.done: each appointed state has an accepted NIPR termination filed on or before its due date, with for-cause narratives transmitted as the state requires.

checklist.step: Send the producer the required written termination notice
actions: Generate the termination notice quoting the states terminated, the effective date and the reason as reported to the state.
Send it to the producer's address of record by the state-required method within the state's notice window (commonly 15 days of filing), keeping the delivery receipt.
Where a state requires the producer to be told of a for-cause report, use the exact language the statute prescribes rather than a paraphrase.
File the notice, the send date and the delivery receipt against the termination task.
checklist.done: each terminated producer has a dated notice sent within the state's window with a retained delivery receipt.

checklist.step: Shut off access, commissions and servicing rights on termination
actions: Disable the producer's portal access and quoting/illustration rights on the termination effective date.
Instruct the Commission Analyst to stop new-business commission and apply the agreement's renewal/vesting treatment for the terminated states.
Reassign the in-force annuity book to a servicing producer who is licensed, appointed and product-trained in each affected state, and notify the affected policyholders.
Record the reassignment and the notification date on the termination task.
checklist.done: access and commissions are stopped on the effective date and the in-force book is reassigned to a qualified servicing producer.

checklist.step: Renew appointments before they lapse
actions: Pull the state appointment renewal invoices and due dates from NIPR Gateway ▸ Appointment Renewals for each state that renews appointments on a calendar cycle.
Reconcile the invoiced appointment list to the active producer roster and drop producers who are no longer writing rather than paying to renew them.
Fund and submit the renewal before the state's due date and record the confirmation.
Flip to Not Eligible any producer whose appointment was deliberately not renewed, on the lapse date.
checklist.done: every renewing state is paid before its due date against a reconciled roster, and non-renewed producers are made ineligible on the lapse date.

checklist.step: Escalate any window that will be missed
actions: Review the overdue and at-risk queues daily: appointments past day 10 of the shortest window and terminations past day 25.
Escalate any for-cause termination at risk of missing its window to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel the same day.
Where a window has already closed, file immediately, record the days late, and decide with counsel whether the state requires a late-filing explanation or fee.
Never re-date a trigger to make a filing look timely.
checklist.done: every at-risk or missed window has a same-day escalation, an immediate filing and a recorded days-late figure.

checklist.step: Reconcile the appointment register to NIPR monthly
actions: Pull the company's full appointment listing per state from NIPR PDB reporting and load it beside the producer management system's appointment table.

Investigate both directions: appointments in NIPR not in the internal register (paying fees for producers you do not have) and internal appointments not in NIPR (business written on an unfiled appointment).
Clear every break with a NIPR transaction or an internal correction and record the resolution.
Report the break count and ageing to the Producer Compliance Manager each month.
checklist.done: the monthly two-way reconciliation is complete with every break resolved and the ageing reported.

checklist.step: Retain appointment and termination evidence
actions: File per NPN per state: NIPR appointment and termination confirmations with transaction ids, rejection notices and resubmissions, for-cause narratives with counsel sign-off, and the producer notice with delivery receipt.
Apply the 5-years-after-appointment-end retention label.
Confirm retrieval by NPN, state, transaction id and termination reason for a DOI appointment audit.
checklist.done: every appointment and termination has a retained, labelled evidence pack retrievable by NPN, state and transaction id.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment and termination trigger events
actions: Extract every producer agreement execution, first-application-in-state event, and producer relationship end date with a trigger date in the quarter.
Add every annuity application in a state where the writing agent had no accepted appointment at signature, so unfiled appointments cannot hide.
Reconcile the trigger count to the NIPR transaction volume for the quarter and explain every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the trigger population reconciles to NIPR transaction volume and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every trigger to an accepted NIPR transaction
actions: Match each trigger to a NIPR appointment or termination transaction on NPN + state + company NAIC code.
Read the submission timestamp and the accepted effective date from the transaction record rather than the internal task.
List unmatched triggers, transactions stuck in Rejected, and terminations with no filing as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every trigger is matched to an accepted NIPR transaction or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations and 100% of triggers in states with a window of 15 days or shorter.
Take 25 further triggers at random (seeded, reproducible) across at least 12 states including Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona, for a minimum of 40 sampled events.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every for-cause termination and every short-window state.

testing.step: Re-derive the state window from source before testing timeliness
actions: For each sampled state, read the appointment and termination windows straight from the state's producer licensing statute and the NIPR state requirement page.
Compare to the day-count table row and treat any difference as a control finding in its own right — a wrong table makes every clock wrong.
Confirm the recorded trigger type (contract execution vs first application) matches what the state actually requires.
Capture the source pages with retrieval dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state's window is independently re-derived from statute and NIPR, with table differences raised as findings.

testing.step: Recompute the day count for every sampled event
actions: Recompute days from the trigger date to the NIPR submission timestamp using the state's day convention (calendar vs business days).
For terminations, separately recompute days from the effective date to the filing and from the filing to the producer notice send date.
Compare to the recorded days-late figure and flag any event where the internal record understates lateness.
Record each recomputation on the workpaper line with the dates relied on.
testing.done: every sampled event has an independently recomputed day count reconciled to the recorded figure.

testing.step: Test for business written before an accepted appointment
actions: For each sampled appointment, list annuity applications signed by that NPN in that state between the trigger date and the accepted effective date.
For states where appointment must precede solicitation, treat every such application as a breach and quantify premium and commission.
For states that back-date the appointment to the trigger, confirm the accepted effective date actually reflects the back-dating.
Capture the application list into the workpaper with policy numbers and premium.
testing.done: pre-appointment business is identified and quantified for every sampled appointment, or confirmed as properly back-dated.

testing.step: Re-perform the for-cause reporting test
actions: Read each sampled for-cause file and confirm the narrative states facts and dates rather than conclusions or characterisations.
Confirm the reported ground maps to a statutory for-cause ground in that state and that the report went by the channel the state requires.
Confirm the producer notice used the statutory language and was sent inside the notice window.
Treat a for-cause event terminated as 'without cause' to avoid the report as a reportable failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled for-cause termination is fact-based, correctly grounded, correctly channelled and properly noticed.

testing.step: Re-perform the NIPR-to-register reconciliation independently
actions: Pull the company's current appointment listing from NIPR PDB reporting for five sampled states and load it beside the internal appointment register.
Count and age breaks in both directions and compare to the latest monthly reconciliation the team produced.
Where the team's reconciliation missed breaks you found, raise the reconciliation control itself as a finding.
Quantify appointment fees paid for producers no longer writing.
testing.done: an independent two-way reconciliation on five states reproduces or challenges the team's break population.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with NPN, state, trigger date, filed date, days late, premium written pre-appointment and the for-cause flag.
Assign a root cause (trigger not detected, day-count table wrong, rejection not worked, fee account unfunded, termination classified to avoid reporting) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and refer missed for-cause reports and pre-appointment business to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report decision.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the within-window rate for appointments and terminations separately and compare to the 99% threshold and the zero-tolerance for-cause threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Licensing Ops, with no sampled NIPR submission of their own — sign the workpaper.
Report results and any self-reports to the Compliance Committee and file under Licensing & Appointments ▸ Appointment Timeliness Test.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with within-window rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
