checklist.step: Build the per-state renewal and CE requirement table
actions: Create one row per jurisdiction with: renewal frequency (usually biennial), renewal anchor (birth month, licence anniversary or fixed date), total CE hours, ethics hours, any line-specific hours, CE reporting method (state, Sircon/Prometric vendor or NIPR) and the grace/reinstatement window.
Add the state's one-time annuity training requirement and any LTC initial and refresher hours to the same row.
Cite the statute or DOI page behind each figure and date the citation.
Publish the table to the producer management system so renewal and CE clocks compute from it, and re-validate annually.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction has a cited row covering renewal anchor, CE hours, ethics hours and annuity/LTC training, driving the system clocks.

checklist.step: Build the rolling renewal calendar for the annuity producer population
actions: Pull every producer flagged Eligible-to-Solicit for Annuity Contracts (non-group) with their per-state licence expiry dates from the latest PDB load.
Generate a rolling 12-month renewal calendar keyed on NPN + state + expiry date, and stratify by producer premium contribution so high-producing agents are chased first.
Cross-check that every state where the producer holds an active appointment appears on the calendar — a renewed resident licence with a lapsed non-resident licence still stops the business.
Publish the calendar to a Power BI dashboard segmented by month, state and channel.
checklist.done: a rolling 12-month renewal calendar covers every NPN/state pair for annuity producers and is visible on the dashboard.

checklist.step: Run the T-120 to T-7 producer chase cadence
actions: Trigger automated notices at T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-7 days to the state expiry date, each naming the state, expiry date, outstanding CE hours and outstanding ethics hours.
Post the producer's live CE gap on the portal landing page so the number the producer sees matches the number Licensing Ops chases.
From T-30 work a call list, logging the call date, who was reached and the commitment made against the NPN.
Escalate to the Agency Relations Manager at T-14 for any producer with hours still outstanding.
checklist.done: every renewal shows the full notice trail plus a logged call from T-30 and an escalation at T-14 where hours remained outstanding.

checklist.step: Verify CE hours at the transcript source, not from producer assertions
actions: Pull the producer's CE transcript from the PDB or the state's CE vendor and read banked hours, ethics hours and the reporting date for the current cycle.
Compare banked hours to the state requirement on the table row and compute the outstanding gap by category.
Confirm each course was approved for that state and falls inside the current cycle dates — hours from a prior cycle do not carry.
Update the renewal log with banked hours, gap and the transcript retrieval date.
checklist.done: each producer's CE position comes from a dated transcript retrieval with the gap computed by hour category.

checklist.step: Verify the one-time state annuity training is still on record
actions: For every annuity-writing producer, confirm the state's annuity suitability/best-interest training credit (commonly a one-time 4-credit course) is recorded and verified at the CE transcript.
Where a state has adopted the best-interest amendments since the producer's original course, check whether a supplemental course is required and assign it.
Reconcile the LMS record to the CE transcript credit — a completion recorded only internally does not satisfy the state.
Report producers lacking a verified credit to the Producer Compliance Manager weekly.
checklist.done: every annuity-writing producer has a transcript-verified state annuity training credit or an assigned supplemental course.

checklist.step: Run the LTC and product refresher cycles
actions: For producers selling annuities with LTC riders, track the state's initial LTC training (commonly 8 hours) and the ongoing refresher (commonly 4 hours every 24 months) with due dates per state.
Track the carrier's own annuity product module refresh cycle and re-assign it whenever the module version changes or the annual refresh falls due.
Set the LMS to block the producer's annuity solicitation eligibility on the day a required refresher goes past due.
Report refresher completion percentage by state and channel monthly.
checklist.done: LTC and carrier product refreshers have per-state due dates, block eligibility when overdue, and are reported monthly.

checklist.step: File the renewal transaction in NIPR before expiry
actions: For company-funded renewals, open NIPR Gateway ▸ License Renewal, select the state and NPN, and confirm CE is satisfied before the state will accept the transaction.
Confirm the renewal fee is funded from the company's NIPR account and submit before the expiry date, not on it.
Record the NIPR transaction id, submission timestamp and the new expiry date on the renewal log.
For producer-funded renewals, confirm completion by re-reading PDB rather than accepting a producer's word.
checklist.done: each renewal has an accepted NIPR transaction with a new expiry date recorded on the log before the old date passed.

checklist.step: Suspend solicitation the day a licence, training or refresher lapses
actions: Run the daily expiry job against the PDB delta and the LMS refresher due dates.
Flip Eligible-to-Solicit to No for the affected state the same day and push the change to the Policy Administration Platform intake edit and the Broker & Agent Portal.
Notify the producer and the Agency Relations Manager in writing with the state, the lapse reason and what is required to restore eligibility.
Never allow a grace-period assumption to keep a producer live — restore eligibility only on a PDB Active status.
checklist.done: every lapse suspends solicitation in that state the same day, with the producer and manager notified in writing.

checklist.step: Work reinstatements inside the state's window
actions: Read the state's reinstatement window and penalty from the requirement table (many states allow reinstatement within 12 months with a late fee, after which re-examination is required).
Confirm the outstanding CE is banked, then submit the reinstatement transaction in NIPR with the late fee funded.
Where the window has closed, restart the producer through pre-licensing education and examination and remove the state from their book until complete.
Record the reinstatement date, fee and new expiry on the renewal log.
checklist.done: each lapse is either reinstated within the state window with the fee recorded, or routed to re-licensing with the state removed from the book.

checklist.step: Quarantine and decide on business written during a lapse
actions: For every lapse, list annuity applications signed by that NPN in that state between the expiry date and the reinstatement date.
Hold the associated commission in the commission platform and quantify premium at risk.
Refer the list to Regulatory Counsel for a decision on validity, re-signature by an eligible producer, or rescission and premium return.
Record the decision and the customer communication on the exception record.
checklist.done: all lapse-window business is identified, commission held, and a counsel decision with a customer outcome is recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile the renewal log to PDB monthly
actions: Load the full PDB licence extract for the roster and compare expiry dates, statuses and lines of authority against the renewal log field by field.
Investigate both directions: licences PDB shows as expired but the log shows renewed, and licences the log does not carry at all.
Clear every break and record the cause (renewal filed but not written back, non-resident licence never loaded, name/NPN mismatch).
Report break count and ageing to the Producer Compliance Manager monthly.
checklist.done: the monthly PDB-to-log reconciliation is complete with every break cleared and its cause recorded.

checklist.step: Report renewal and CE health to distribution leadership
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard: renewals due next 120 days by state and channel, CE gap in hours, on-time renewal rate, current lapses and premium exposed.
Show the top 20 producers by premium with any outstanding CE, annuity training or refresher gap by name and NPN.
Take the Head of Distribution's committed remediation actions and dates into the tracker.
Trend on-time renewal rate against the 98% threshold across the last eight quarters.
checklist.done: distribution leadership receives a monthly dashboard with named at-risk producers and committed remediation dates.

checklist.step: Refresh the requirement table when a state changes CE or annuity training rules
actions: Monitor state DOI bulletin feeds and NAIC model adoption notices for changes to CE hours, ethics credit, annuity best-interest training and LTC refresher rules.
Within 10 business days of a change, update the affected requirement rows, re-date the citations and note the effective date of the change.
Recompute the affected producers' CE and training gaps and issue the delta to Licensing Ops as a chase list.
Record the change and the population impacted on the change log.
checklist.done: every state rule change is reflected in the table within 10 business days with a recomputed producer chase list issued.

checklist.step: Escalate producers who will miss the renewal date
actions: At T-14, list producers whose outstanding CE hours cannot realistically be completed and banked before expiry given the state's CE reporting lag.
Escalate to the Head of Distribution with the premium at risk and the states that will close.
Agree the servicing plan for the in-force annuity book in states about to lapse and record the receiving producer.
Record the decision and owner against each NPN.
checklist.done: every producer forecast to miss renewal has an escalation, a premium-at-risk figure and a named servicing plan.

checklist.step: Retain the renewal and CE evidence
actions: File per NPN per state: renewal confirmations with NIPR transaction ids, dated CE transcripts, course certificates, annuity and LTC training records, and the chase/notice trail.
Apply the 5-years-after-renewal-date retention label.
Confirm retrieval by NPN, state, renewal date and course type for a DOI producer-qualification request.
checklist.done: every renewal cycle has a retained, labelled evidence pack retrievable by NPN, state and renewal date.

testing.step: Build the population of renewals, CE deadlines and training refreshes due
actions: Extract every NPN/state licence with an expiry date in the quarter, plus every CE cycle end and every LTC or product refresher due date in the quarter, for annuity-writing producers.
Add producers who wrote annuity business in the quarter but do not appear on the renewal calendar, to catch non-resident licences never loaded.
Reconcile the extract to the PDB roster count and clear differences before sampling.
testing.done: the renewal/CE/refresher population reconciles to the PDB roster and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every due item to an outcome in PDB
actions: For each due renewal, read the PDB status and the current expiry date and classify it renewed on time, renewed late, lapsed, or intentionally not renewed.
For each CE deadline, read banked hours and ethics hours on the transcript at the cycle end date.
List every item with no PDB outcome, a lapse, or a CE shortfall at cycle end as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every due item carries a PDB-sourced outcome classification or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of lapses in the quarter and 100% of the top 20 producers by annuity premium with a renewal or refresher due.
Take 25 further NPN/state renewals at random (seeded, reproducible) across at least 10 states including Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona, for a minimum of 40 sampled items.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every lapse and every high-premium producer with a due item.

testing.step: Re-derive each sampled state's renewal and CE requirement from source
actions: Read the renewal frequency, anchor date, total CE hours, ethics hours and annuity training requirement straight from the state DOI page and the licensing statute.
Compare to the requirement table row and raise any difference as a control finding — a wrong table silently under-chases the whole state.
Confirm the state's CE reporting lag assumption used in the chase cadence is realistic.
Capture the source pages with retrieval dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state's requirements are independently re-derived from source with table differences raised as findings.

testing.step: Re-perform the CE verification on the sample
actions: Pull the PDB CE transcript for each sampled NPN and independently total banked hours and ethics hours for the cycle.
Confirm each counted course was approved in that state and completed inside the cycle window.
Compare your totals to the renewal log figure; a shortfall recorded as satisfied is an exception even where the state still renewed the licence.
Capture the transcript into the workpaper with its retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled CE position is independently totalled from the transcript and reconciled to the renewal log.

testing.step: Trace the state annuity and LTC training to a verified credit
actions: For each sampled annuity producer, verify the state annuity training credit at the CE transcript or the approved provider's portal rather than the LMS record.
Where the state adopted best-interest amendments, confirm any required supplemental training was completed before continued solicitation.
For LTC-rider sellers, confirm the initial hours and the current refresher are both in date.
Any credit that cannot be verified at source, or a refresher past due while the producer kept soliciting, is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled annuity and LTC training credit is source-verified and in date for the solicitation that occurred.

testing.step: Test the same-day suspension control on lapses
actions: For each sampled lapse, compute elapsed business days between the PDB expiry/delta date and the Eligible-to-Solicit flip to No.
Confirm the flip propagated to the Policy Administration Platform intake edit and the Broker & Agent Portal quoting tools on the same day.
Attempt a negative test with a lapsed test NPN and confirm the annuity application and the portal quote are both refused.
Capture the reject screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled lapse suspended within the same business day and propagation to intake and portal is evidenced.

testing.step: Quantify business written during lapse windows
actions: For every lapse in the population, list annuity applications signed by that NPN in that state between expiry and reinstatement, with premium and commission.
Confirm commission was held in the commission platform and that a counsel decision exists on validity or rescission.
Recompute the reinstatement date against the state's reinstatement window to confirm the producer was eligible to be reinstated at all.
Any lapse-window business without a counsel decision is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: all lapse-window business is quantified with commission held and a counsel decision evidenced.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with NPN, state, expiry date, days lapsed, CE shortfall by hour category, premium written while lapsed and commission held.
Assign a root cause (state not on the calendar, requirement table stale, chase cadence not run, CE reporting lag underestimated, suspension not propagated) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and refer lapse-window business to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report decision.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time renewal rate and the training-in-date rate and compare to the 98% and zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Licensing Ops, with no involvement in any sampled chase or filing — sign the workpaper.
Report results, lapse-window exposure and self-report decisions to the Compliance Committee and file under Licensing & Appointments ▸ Renewal & CE Test.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time renewal rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the 18 U.S.C. §1033 prohibited-person screening gate for every new hire and newly contracted annuity producer, and the §1034 written-consent file where one is needed

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 18 U.S.C. §1033 (prohibited persons in the business of insurance) and §1034 (civil enforcement / commissioner's written consent), read with each state's producer background and fingerprint requirements and its producer product-training rule (rep: Alabama Department of Insurance (ALDOI); Arkansas and Arizona screened on the same standard)

In-scope processes.value: Pre-engagement screening: employee hire into any insurance-business role and producer contracting for Annuity Contracts (non-group) — criminal history and fingerprint check, §1033 self-attestation, PDB regulatory-action review, sanctions/adverse-media check, and §1034 consent tracking, in all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Background and adverse-media screening; NIPR PDB Regulatory Actions for producer history; §1033 attestations and consent orders filed in the compliance evidence repository; hire-side records in the HRIS

Compliance procedure documented.value: 1033 Screening & Prohibited Person Procedure — attestation wording, disqualifying-offence definitions (felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust, or an offence under Chapter 47 of Title 18), adjudication matrix, §1034 consent application route, and the annual re-attestation cycle

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance, Employment Counsel and Regulatory Counsel; re-approved annually and on any change to state fingerprinting or background-check requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per hire / per contracting — screening must clear before the start date or before the producer agreement is counter-signed; a §1034 written-consent application must be filed before the person engages in the business of insurance, and self-disclosure of a new conviction is required immediately and in any event within 5 business days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Screening case SLA alerts at day 3, day 7 and day 10 from initiation; annual re-attestation campaign opens 60 days before the anniversary with reminders at day 30, day 14 and day 3; open consent applications reviewed monthly

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed §1033 attestations, background and fingerprint results, PDB regulatory-action captures, adjudication decisions and any commissioner's written consent retained 7 years after the engagement ends, in a restricted-access folder

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any person engaged in the business of insurance without a cleared screening, and any identified prohibited person without a §1034 consent, is logged with the individual, role, engagement dates and the removal or consent action taken

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every adjudication that permits engagement despite an adverse finding and every §1034 consent application before it is filed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All employee hires and all producer contracting approvals in the quarter, plus every PDB regulatory action and self-disclosed conviction reported in the quarter for the existing population

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — one person engaged in the business of insurance without a cleared screening on or before the engagement date, or one prohibited person engaged without a written §1034 consent, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per hire and per contracting; screening completeness is monitored monthly and the sample-based test runs quarterly over that quarter's hires and contracting approvals

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in Compliance screening or HR recruiting and must not have adjudicated any sampled case

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly §1033 screening test workpaper (hire and contracting population, screening traces, adjudication re-performance, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under restricted access

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Screening register with per-person attestation, background result date, adjudication decision and any consent order reference, producible for a state DOI or market conduct background-screening request within 10 business days, redacted per data-protection rules

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance answers §1033/§1034 enquiries with Regulatory Counsel; Employment Counsel clears any adverse-action communication to an individual before it is sent

checklist.step: Define who is in scope for §1033 screening
actions: Write the in-scope population as: every employee whose role touches the business of insurance (underwriting, claims, annuity new business, suitability review, distribution, licensing, actuarial, compliance) and every producer or agency contracting to sell Annuity Contracts (non-group).
Include contingent workers, offshore vendor staff with policy or claim system access, and agency principals — §1033 reaches anyone engaged in the business of insurance, not only payrolled staff.
Agree the list with the Chief HR Officer and Employment Counsel and record who is explicitly out of scope and why.
Publish the scope statement and re-confirm it annually.
checklist.done: the in-scope population is written, agreed with HR and Employment Counsel, and the out-of-scope exclusions are justified in writing.

checklist.step: Trigger a screening case at offer and at contracting
actions: On every conditional offer for an in-scope role, raise a screening case carrying candidate name, role, legal entity, work location and planned start date.
Make the start date in the HRIS unconfirmable until the screening case status reads Cleared — the system, not a manager's memory, holds the gate.
For producer contracting, have the Producer Licensing Coordinator raise the equivalent case at contracting intake keyed on the NPN.
Set the case SLA clock from the trigger date with alerts at day 3, 7 and 10.
checklist.done: every in-scope offer and contracting intake has a screening case open with an SLA clock and a system-enforced start-date gate.

checklist.step: Collect the signed §1033 attestation
actions: Send the §1033 attestation asking, in the statute's own terms, whether the person has ever been convicted of any criminal felony involving dishonesty or a breach of trust, or of an offence under Chapter 47 of Title 18, and whether they have ever been the subject of an insurance regulatory action.
Require a Yes/No answer per question plus a free-text explanation for any Yes, with dates, jurisdiction, charge and disposition.
Capture the signature with an audit trail and timestamp; refuse unsigned or partially completed attestations rather than chasing later.
File the executed attestation against the screening case.
checklist.done: an executed, fully answered attestation with a signature audit trail sits on the screening case.

checklist.step: Run the criminal history and fingerprint checks the state requires
actions: Order a national and county-level criminal history search covering every jurisdiction of residence for the past 7 years, plus a federal district court search for Chapter 47 offences.
Where the state requires fingerprinting for licensure, confirm the producer's fingerprint submission and the state's response are complete via NIPR or the state vendor before contracting.
Run OFAC/sanctions and adverse-media screening on the same identity and record the screening reference and date.
Attach all result documents to the screening case and never accept a candidate-supplied copy as the result of record.
checklist.done: criminal history, federal, fingerprint (where required) and sanctions results are on the case from the provider directly, with dates.

checklist.step: Review the PDB regulatory-action history for every producer
actions: Run the PDB report by NPN and open Regulatory Actions, reading every action's state, date, allegation and disposition.
Read the Licenses section for any state showing Suspended, Revoked or Surrendered and record which states and when.
Where an action exists, obtain the underlying consent order or DOI order from the state's public records rather than relying on the PDB summary line.
Attach the actions and orders to the screening case and flag it for adjudication.
checklist.done: every producer case carries a PDB regulatory-action review with the underlying orders attached where actions exist.

checklist.step: Adjudicate findings against the disqualification matrix
actions: For each finding, decide whether the offence is a felony, whether it involved dishonesty or breach of trust, or whether it falls under Chapter 47 of Title 18 — those three tests, not the severity of the story.
Record the charge, statute, conviction date, jurisdiction and disposition, and state the reasoning for the conclusion on the case.
Where the answer is Prohibited, do not engage the person in the business of insurance without a §1034 written consent — an internal risk assessment is not a substitute.
Where the answer is Not Prohibited, still assess fitness and propriety with Employment Counsel and record that separate conclusion.
checklist.done: every finding has a documented three-test conclusion with the underlying offence detail and a separate fitness decision.

checklist.step: Apply the adverse-action process before declining anyone
actions: Where a background result may cause a decline, issue the pre-adverse-action notice with a copy of the report and the summary of rights, and hold the statutory waiting period open for dispute.
Consider state and local fair-chance and ban-the-box restrictions on how and when conviction history may be used.
Where the person disputes the record, pause the case until the provider re-investigates and reissues.
Issue the final adverse-action notice only after the waiting period and record the dates of both notices on the case.
checklist.done: no decline is issued without a documented pre-adverse notice, waiting period and final notice with dates on the case.

checklist.step: File a §1034 written-consent application where the company wants to engage a prohibited person
actions: Identify the correct commissioner — the domiciliary state's insurance commissioner for the entity the person will work in — and read that state's consent application requirements.
Assemble the application: the individual's statement, certified court records of the conviction, the proposed role and its controls, character references and the company's supervision plan.
File and diary the state's response window; the person may not engage in the business of insurance in the meantime.
On receipt, file the consent order, record its scope and any conditions on the screening case, and diary any renewal or reporting condition.
checklist.done: each prohibited person the company intends to engage has a filed consent application and, if granted, a filed consent order with its conditions diarised.

checklist.step: Record the screening outcome and release the engagement gate
actions: Set the case status to Cleared, Cleared with consent, or Not Cleared, with the decision date and the decider named.
Push Cleared to the HRIS so the start date can be confirmed, and to the producer management system so contracting can proceed to licence verification.
For Not Cleared, ensure no system access, no NPN contracting record and no appointment request can proceed, and notify the hiring manager without disclosing the underlying report content.
Write the outcome to the screening register with the evidence references.
checklist.done: each case has a named decision with a date, propagated to HRIS and producer contracting, and the register updated.

checklist.step: Bind ongoing self-disclosure into the contract and handbook
actions: Include in the producer agreement and the employee handbook an obligation to notify the company immediately, and in any event within 5 business days, of any criminal charge, conviction or insurance regulatory action.
State the consequence explicitly: engagement ceases pending adjudication and a §1034 consent where the conviction is disqualifying.
Confirm the clause is present in the current template version and in the executed agreements for the population contracted this year.
Log the template version and its effective date.
checklist.done: the current producer agreement and handbook both carry the 5-business-day self-disclosure obligation with its stated consequence.

checklist.step: Run the annual re-attestation and continuous monitoring cycle
actions: Open the annual §1033 re-attestation campaign 60 days before each person's anniversary, with reminders at day 30, 14 and 3.
Subscribe the producer roster to NIPR Alerts so new regulatory actions arrive without waiting for the anniversary.
Re-run sanctions and adverse-media screening on the whole in-scope population at least annually and on any Yes answer.
Suspend anyone who fails to attest by the anniversary date and record the suspension.
checklist.done: every in-scope person re-attests annually, PDB alerts are live, and non-attesters are suspended on the anniversary date.

checklist.step: Handle a new conviction or regulatory action on an existing person
actions: On any self-disclosure, PDB alert or adverse-media hit, open a screening case the same day and suspend the person's access, solicitation eligibility and commission.
Adjudicate against the same three tests and, where prohibited, remove them from the business of insurance immediately pending any §1034 consent.
Assess whether a state appointment termination is now for cause and hand it to Licensing Ops with the counsel-cleared narrative.
Notify the Head of Compliance the same day for any prohibited-person finding on an engaged individual.
checklist.done: each new conviction or action has a same-day case, suspension, adjudication and a termination-classification decision.

checklist.step: Extend screening to agencies, FMOs and vendor staff
actions: Require in every agency, FMO and BPO contract a warranty that the counterparty screens its own staff against §1033 and will not place a prohibited person on the company's business.
Obtain an annual attestation from each counterparty naming the screening standard used and the population covered.
Sample-test counterparty screening evidence for the two largest agencies and any counterparty with system access each year.
Log the attestations and test results in the third-party risk register.
checklist.done: every agency, FMO and vendor with insurance-business staff has a contractual §1033 warranty and a current annual attestation.

checklist.step: Protect the screening data
actions: Restrict the screening folder to named Compliance and Employment Counsel users and evidence the access list quarterly.
Confirm background reports and attestations are not copied into HRIS free-text notes, recruiting records or email threads.
Apply the retention rule (7 years after the engagement ends) and confirm automatic disposal is configured.
Log any access review exception and remove the access the same day.
checklist.done: screening records are restricted to a named list, evidenced quarterly, with retention and disposal configured.

checklist.step: Retain the screening evidence pack
actions: File per person: signed attestation, background and fingerprint results, PDB regulatory-action capture, adjudication decision with reasoning, adverse-action notices and any §1034 consent order.
Apply the 7-years-after-engagement-ends retention label in the restricted folder.
Confirm retrieval by person, NPN or employee id, engagement date and outcome for a DOI background-screening request.
checklist.done: every screened person has a retained, restricted, labelled evidence pack retrievable by identifier and outcome.

testing.step: Build the population of engagements requiring screening
actions: Extract every hire, rehire and internal move into an in-scope role in the quarter with name, employee id, role, legal entity and start date.
Extract every producer and agency contracting approval in the quarter from the producer management system with NPN and approval date.

Add contingent workers and vendor staff granted policy or claim system access in the quarter from the IAM joiner report, then reconcile the combined count to payroll and contracting reports before sampling.
testing.done: the engagement population covers employees, producers and contingent/vendor staff and reconciles to payroll and contracting reports.

testing.step: Reconcile every engagement to a cleared screening case pre-dating it
actions: Match each engagement to a screening case on employee id or NPN and read the case status and decision date.
Check the decision date is on or before the start date or the producer agreement counter-signature date.
List engagements with no case, a case cleared after engagement, or a case still open as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every engagement matches a screening case cleared on or before engagement, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of cases with any Yes answer on the attestation, any PDB regulatory action, any adverse background finding, and 100% of §1034 consent files.
Take 25 clean cases at random (seeded, reproducible) split across employees and producers, for a minimum of 40 sampled cases.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every adverse finding and every consent file.

testing.step: Re-perform the attestation completeness check
actions: Open the executed attestation for each sampled case and confirm every question is answered, the signature audit trail is present and the signature date pre-dates engagement.
Confirm the wording still tracks §1033 — felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust and Chapter 47 offences — rather than a paraphrase that could let a disqualifying conviction through.
Check every Yes answer carries the date, jurisdiction, charge and disposition detail the procedure requires.
Capture the attestation into the workpaper with any redaction the data-protection rules require.
testing.done: each sampled attestation is complete, correctly worded, pre-dated and detailed on every Yes answer.

testing.step: Trace background, fingerprint and sanctions results to the provider record
actions: For each sampled case, open the provider's result record directly and compare the search scope (jurisdictions, years, federal district coverage) to the procedure's requirement.
Confirm the result date pre-dates engagement and that the identity searched matches the person engaged, including former names.
For producers in fingerprint states, confirm the fingerprint response is on file from NIPR or the state vendor.
Treat a candidate-supplied copy standing in for the provider record as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled case traces to a provider-sourced result of the required scope, pre-dating engagement, on the right identity.

testing.step: Re-perform the PDB regulatory-action review on sampled producers
actions: Run a fresh PDB report by NPN and read Regulatory Actions and Licenses independently of the case file.
Compare what you find to what the case recorded; an action present in PDB but absent from the case is an exception regardless of its severity.
For actions found, confirm the underlying state order was obtained and read rather than the PDB summary alone.
Capture the PDB Regulatory Actions section with its retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled producer's PDB action history is independently re-read and reconciled to the case file.

testing.step: Re-perform the disqualification adjudication
actions: For each adverse finding, read the underlying court or DOI record and independently apply the three tests: felony, dishonesty or breach of trust, Chapter 47 offence.
Compare to the recorded conclusion; a correct outcome supported by wrong reasoning is still an exception because it will not repeat reliably.
Where the conclusion was Prohibited, confirm no engagement occurred without a granted §1034 consent covering the actual role.
Confirm the consent order's conditions are diarised and being met.
testing.done: every adverse finding is independently adjudicated and every prohibited person is covered by a granted, condition-tracked consent.

testing.step: Test the engagement gate and the annual re-attestation cycle
actions: Attempt to confirm a start date in the HRIS for a test candidate whose screening case is not Cleared and confirm the system refuses.
Attempt to progress a producer contracting record to appointment with an open screening case and confirm the producer management system blocks it.
Recompute the annual re-attestation population from anniversaries in the period and compare to the campaign's actual sent and completed counts.
Confirm every non-attester past their anniversary was suspended, with the suspension date evidenced.
testing.done: both engagement gates refuse ineligible cases and the re-attestation population, completion and suspensions reconcile.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the person identifier, role, engagement date, the missing or defective screening element and the exposure period.
Assign a root cause (case not raised, gate bypassed, scope excluded the role, provider scope too narrow, adjudication reasoning wrong, re-attestation not run) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date, remove any prohibited person from the business of insurance immediately, and refer to Regulatory Counsel for a §1034 or self-report decision.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, an immediate removal where required and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the screening completeness rate and the adjudication accuracy rate and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Compliance screening and HR recruiting — sign the workpaper.
Report results and any prohibited-person findings to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the restricted §1033 folder.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with completeness and accuracy rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the restricted folder.

checklist.step: Fix the reconciliation as-of date and freeze the inputs
actions: Set the as-of date to the last calendar day of the quarter and require every extract to be pulled against that date, not the pull date.
Name the three inputs: NIPR appointment/licence extract, internal producer and appointment roster, and the quarter's annuity commission-paid population.
Confirm the writing-company list (NAIC codes) in scope so no company is silently omitted from the NIPR pull.
Open the quarter's reconciliation task with the 20-business-day completion date and the break ageing thresholds.
checklist.done: the as-of date, the three inputs, the company list and the completion date are recorded on the quarter's reconciliation task.

checklist.step: Pull the NIPR appointment and licence extract for every writing company
actions: In NIPR Gateway open PDB Reports / Appointment Reporting and request the company appointment listing per state for each NAIC company code in scope.
Request the companion licence status extract by NPN so licence expiry and lines of authority sit alongside the appointment rows.
Check the file control totals (record count per state) against the report header before loading; a short file silently manufactures breaks.
Save the extracts unedited as <company>-<state>-NIPR-<as-of date>.csv into the reconciliation folder.
checklist.done: unedited NIPR appointment and licence extracts for every writing company are saved with control totals verified.

checklist.step: Pull the internal roster and appointment table at the same as-of date
actions: Extract every producer/state row with NPN, producer name, writing company, appointment status and effective date, licence status, Eligible-to-Solicit flag and contract status as at the as-of date.
Use the point-in-time view rather than the current view — a producer terminated after quarter-end must still appear as appointed at quarter-end.
Include agency/firm entities as their own rows, since firm appointments reconcile separately from individual ones.
Record the extract row count and timestamp on the reconciliation task.
checklist.done: a point-in-time internal roster extract at the as-of date is saved with its row count and timestamp recorded.

checklist.step: Pull the commission-paid population for the quarter
actions: Extract every annuity commission payment in the quarter with NPN, payee, policy number, policy situs state, premium and commission amount.
Roll it up to distinct NPN + state pairs with total commission, so the reconciliation can test the compensation question directly.
Include overrides paid to agency and FMO entities, which carry their own appointment requirements in many states.
Reconcile total commission in the extract to the general ledger commission expense for the quarter before handing it over.
checklist.done: the commission population is extracted, rolled to NPN/state pairs including overrides, and tied to the GL commission expense.

checklist.step: Match the three populations on NPN, state and company
actions: Join NIPR to internal on NPN + state + NAIC company code; never match on producer name, which breaks on marriages, suffixes and agency DBAs.
Left-join the commission pairs onto the matched set so every paid pair carries its appointment and licence position.
Report the match rate and the count of unmatched rows on each side before any interpretation.
Save the matched workbook with the join keys and formulas intact so the match can be re-performed.
checklist.done: the three populations are joined on NPN + state + company with a reported match rate and a re-performable workbook.

checklist.step: Classify every break into a named category
actions: Category A — appointment in NIPR, none internally: fee being paid for a producer the company no longer uses, or a termination never filed internally.
Category B — appointment internally, none in NIPR: production may be running on an unfiled appointment; treat as the highest severity.
Category C — appointment present both sides but licence expired or lines insufficient in PDB.
Category D — commission paid with no appointment or no active licence in the situs state; Category E — data-only breaks (name, NPN, entity-type mismatch).
Write the category, the evidence and the affected premium/commission onto each break row.
checklist.done: every break carries a category, its evidence and the premium or commission exposed.

checklist.step: Quantify the exposure behind Category B and D breaks
actions: For each Category B and D break, list the annuity applications signed in that state by that NPN during the exposure window with policy number, signature date and premium.
Total premium and commission per break and mark whether policies are still in force.
Check whether the producer held the carrier annuity product training and the state annuity training at the time — an unappointed producer who was also untrained is a compounded breach.
Attach the policy list to the break row.
checklist.done: every Category B and D break has a policy list, premium and commission total, and a training position at the time of sale.

checklist.step: Resolve Category A breaks and stop the fee waste
actions: For each Category A break, confirm the producer relationship really has ended by checking the contract status and the last commission payment date.
Where ended, submit the NIPR termination for the state and record the transaction id — an unterminated appointment keeps incurring renewal fees and keeps the company answerable for the producer.
Where the producer is genuinely still active, correct the internal roster and record the data cause.
Total the annual appointment fees avoided and report it with the reconciliation.
checklist.done: every Category A break is either terminated in NIPR with a transaction id or corrected internally, with fee savings quantified.

checklist.step: Resolve Category B and C breaks immediately
actions: For Category B, verify the licence in PDB, then file the appointment in NIPR the same day with the correct effective date and record the days the state was exposed.
For Category C, suspend Eligible-to-Solicit in that state the same day and put the producer into the renewal/CE chase, restoring only on a PDB Active status.
Where the state requires the appointment to have preceded solicitation, hand the exposure list to Regulatory Counsel rather than quietly back-filing.
Record the resolution, transaction id and date on the break row.
checklist.done: every Category B appointment is filed and every Category C producer suspended on the day the break is identified.

checklist.step: Hold and recover commission on Category D breaks
actions: Place the affected NPN/state commission on hold and stop future payments until the appointment and licence position is corrected.
Compute the recoverable amount for periods where no licence existed — many states prohibit paying commission to an unlicensed person outright.
Process chargebacks or offsets against future commission per the producer agreement, and notify the producer in writing with the calculation.
Record the held, recovered and written-off amounts against the break.
checklist.done: every Category D break has commission held, a computed recoverable amount and a recorded recovery or write-off decision.

checklist.step: Fix the root cause behind data-only breaks
actions: Group Category E breaks by cause: NPN missing or mistyped, name changed at the state but not internally, individual record used where the state appointed the firm, duplicate producer records.
Fix the master data, merge duplicates on NPN and add a validation that rejects a producer record without a PDB-resolving NPN.
Re-run the affected joins to confirm the break clears rather than assuming the fix worked.
Report the recurring causes to the Producer Compliance Manager for the control-improvement list.
checklist.done: data-only breaks are fixed at the master-data level, re-tested, and their recurring causes reported.

checklist.step: Age and escalate unresolved breaks
actions: Age every open break from the identification date and alert at 15 and 30 days.
Escalate any Category B or D break open beyond 30 days to the Head of Compliance with the premium and commission exposed.
Refer any pattern — a state, an agency or a channel producing repeat breaks — for a targeted review of that population rather than row-by-row fixes.
Record every escalation with its decision and owner.
checklist.done: no break passes 30 days without an escalation and an approved disposition, and repeat patterns are referred for targeted review.

checklist.step: Produce and sign the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Report per state: NIPR appointment count, internal count, match rate, breaks by category, premium and commission exposed, fees avoided and open break ageing.
Compare the break rate to the 0.5% threshold and state whether the quarter passed.
Have the Head of Compliance sign the report and record the signature date.
Present it to the Compliance Committee with the aged Category B and D breaks named.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly report exists showing per-state counts, break categories, exposure and the threshold outcome.

checklist.step: Feed the findings back into the daily controls
actions: Translate each recurring break cause into a preventative control change: a tighter intake edit, an extra NIPR delta field, a firm-vs-individual appointment rule, or an extra step in the appointment procedure.
Agree the change, the owner and the delivery date with the Head of Distribution and the Business Systems Analyst.
Confirm at the following quarter's reconciliation whether the break category actually shrank; where it did not, escalate the control change as ineffective.
Update the Appointment & Termination Processing Procedure with any new step.
checklist.done: every recurring break category has an owned preventative control change with a delivery date and a next-quarter effectiveness check.

checklist.step: Retain the reconciliation evidence
actions: File the unedited NIPR extracts, the internal point-in-time extract, the commission extract, the matched workbook, the break log with resolutions and the signed report.
Apply the 7-years-from-reconciliation-date retention label.
Confirm retrieval by quarter, state, NAIC company code and NPN so a market conduct appointment audit can be answered directly from the pack.
checklist.done: each quarter's reconciliation pack is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by quarter, state, company and NPN.

testing.step: Pull independent extracts rather than accepting the team's files
actions: Request your own NIPR appointment and licence extract for the same as-of date and the same NAIC company codes, straight from NIPR Gateway PDB Reporting.
Request an independent point-in-time roster extract from the producer management system through IT rather than from Licensing Ops.
Compare record counts to the team's inputs; any difference in the inputs invalidates the reconciliation before you look at a single break.
Record both extract timestamps and control totals in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent NIPR and roster extracts exist at the same as-of date with counts compared to the team's inputs.

testing.step: Re-perform the match and reconcile the break population
actions: Re-join your extracts on NPN + state + NAIC company code and produce your own break list by category.
Reconcile your break count to the team's break log and investigate every difference in both directions.
Confirm the team matched on NPN and not on producer name, which would hide agency and name-change breaks.
List breaks the team missed as findings against the reconciliation control itself.
testing.done: an independent break population is produced and reconciled to the team's break log with every difference explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of breaks and clean rows
actions: Take 100% of Category B and Category D breaks and 100% of breaks aged beyond 30 days.
Take 25 rows the reconciliation reported as clean, at random (seeded, reproducible), across at least 10 states including Alabama, Arkansas and Arizona.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample covers every high-severity and aged break plus a random clean-row stratum, and is reproducible.

testing.step: Re-verify sampled clean rows directly in the PDB
actions: For each sampled clean row, run a PDB report by NPN and read the appointment status, effective date, licence status and lines of authority for that state and company.
Reach your own conclusion before opening the reconciliation workbook; a row marked clean that is actually a break is the most damaging finding available.
Confirm the lines of authority support annuity solicitation, not merely a live licence.
Capture the PDB screens with retrieval dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled clean row is independently confirmed in the PDB or reclassified as a missed break.

testing.step: Trace Category B and D exposure to real policies and payments
actions: For each sampled Category B and D break, pull the annuity applications signed by that NPN in that state during the exposure window with signature dates and premium.
Trace the commission actually paid on those policies in the commission platform and compare to the amount the break row claims.
Confirm the producer's carrier product training and state annuity training position at the signature date.
Any understatement of exposure in the break log is a finding in its own right.
testing.done: sampled high-severity breaks are traced to real policies and payments with the exposure figure independently confirmed.

testing.step: Recompute the commission recovery and hold decisions
actions: Recompute the recoverable commission for each sampled Category D break from the payment records and the exposure window dates.
Confirm the hold was actually applied and that no further payment was released before the appointment and licence were corrected.
Confirm each write-off has a named approver within delegated authority.
Compare the total recovered to what the quarterly report claimed.
testing.done: recoverable commission is independently recomputed, holds are confirmed applied, and write-offs carry authorised approvers.

testing.step: Test resolution timeliness and ageing discipline
actions: Recompute days from break identification to resolution for every sampled break and compare to the 30-day standard.
Confirm Category B appointments were filed and Category C producers suspended on the identification date itself, not later in the cycle.
Confirm every break aged past 30 days carries a Head of Compliance disposition with a date.
Check that breaks reported as resolved actually cleared in the following quarter's reconciliation rather than reappearing.
testing.done: resolution timeliness is recomputed, same-day actions are evidenced, and resolved breaks are confirmed not to have recurred.

testing.step: Assess whether the reconciliation itself was performed on time and completely
actions: Confirm the extracts were pulled at the correct as-of date and the reconciliation completed within 20 business days of quarter-end.
Confirm every NAIC company code and every jurisdiction where business was written appears in the reconciliation scope.
Confirm the commission extract tied to the GL commission expense before it was used.
A reconciliation missing a company, a state or the GL tie is a scope failure regardless of its break rate.
testing.done: timing, company and jurisdiction scope, and the GL tie are all confirmed, or a scope failure is raised.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the NPN, state, company code, break category, exposure window, premium and commission, and whether it was missed by the original reconciliation.
Assign a root cause (name-based matching, missing company from the NIPR pull, current-view instead of point-in-time roster, break aged without disposition, commission not held) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and refer unappointed production and unlicensed compensation to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report decision.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the break rate on your independent population and compare it to the 0.5% threshold and to the rate the team reported.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding, calling out any break the team missed.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Licensing Ops, with no break clearance of their own in the quarter — sign the workpaper.
Report results, unappointed-production exposure and self-report decisions to the Compliance Committee and file under Licensing & Appointments ▸ Roster Reconciliation Test.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an independent break rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
